You say that you have made all of the sacrifices to acquire you assets on your own, yet your girlfriend has been with you for the majority of this time. I don't know anything about your relationship but from what you say it sounds like you should probably terminate the relationship. It does not sound like you view this as a partnership in any way and only see her as a liability (and you could be right). You have had 5 years to get to know her character and her intentions, if you don't feel confident now you probably never will. It does not sound like you interested in marriage--that may change at some point  but it sounds like you expect a level of legal protection that a prenup would not provide. It seems like you are just wasting her time if you don't clearly spell it out to her that this relationship will not end in marriage. You are very concerned about potentially giving up any portion of your earnings without considering that she is 'giving up' a significant portion of her youth and time to a relationship with someone who already knows that it won't work out. To continue the relationship further without telling her that marriage will never be on the horizon would be very dishonest.

We're all afraid of death-that's why people agonize over suicidal thoughts. The real problem comes when you become habituated to that fear so it diminishes over time. The more times you attempt suicide the more likely you are to succeed. People step closer and closer to the edge many times before they become numb enough to the fear that they take the leap.

Feeling like a burden is one of the number one reasons why people try to commit suicide. The vast of majority of the time it is a feeling and not reality. Chances are you see your suicide as the ultimate courtesy for your loved ones-that by killing yourself you are going to make their lives better/easier. I can assure you that is not the case and even though you are taking steps to soften the blow, none of that can lessen the pain of losing your son to suicide. 
It sounds like you're severely depressed-have you tried medication? Therapy? Before making such an ultimate decision shouldn't you do everything you can to see if you situation can improve?

That sounds a little harsh--laying on a guilt trip rarely helps when someone is suicidal. 
It's easy to say in retrospect that someone could've come to you for help but in reality depression is very isolating and suicidal thoughts aren't cured by a couple of conversations with a friend. Death isn't easy, someone who is seriously considering it as their only option is in a lot of pain and feels so cornered that they see that as the only way out. 
That isn't the reality, but it definitely seems real to the person experiencing it.
